# Architect rulings - S4-05 stored demonstration provenance (2026-10-15)

Authority: `tasks/S4-05-stored-demo-provenance.md`, `I-stored-demo-provenance`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q3, `D-2026-10-15-lr01-source-time-cohort`, `D-2026-10-15-s501-finding-choice`, and the owner's absence delegation. These are implementation decisions, not owner approval of visible copy or pilot designation.

## Q1 - authoritative publication moment: accept with transaction detail

The only authoritative authored-demonstration designation is a server-authorized SYSTEM publication committed **before** admission of its exact Batch V2. Pin tenant/Site UUID, gateway/source, external batch ID, canonical payload SHA-256, immutable publication ID and fixture/spec ID/version. Resolve service principal, authorization basis, channel, trigger and recorded time on the server. An identical registration retry returns the same ID; changed content or reuse of a publication ID fails. A gateway credential, client text, `SIMULATED`, Site/day match or missing designation proves no authorship.

Registration and `open_batch` must take the same transaction-scoped lock on the scoped batch key and check for an existing batch while holding it. Registration after any batch admission fails, including a partially completed batch. `open_batch` binds at most the exact preauthorized commitment in its admission transaction; a matching-key but mismatched commitment fails rather than silently becoming unknown. Accepted IDs inherit that immutable binding, including after chunk restart. Duplicates retain their original accepted ID and provenance; rejected/conflict rows acquire none. Existing accepted rows remain unknown, with no retrospective spec/date backfill. The fixture command stays server-side with an explicit configured authority; no public designation route.

**Packet change:** spell out the shared lock key/transaction, registration-after-partial-admission refusal, and mismatch failure in the phase-1 contract/tests. Show the P01 positive path as fresh publication followed by upload of that exact new batch.

## Q2 - several publications in one Finding: accept with set definition

Several distinct authored publication IDs may support one selected FindingRevision if **every** cited accepted ID resolves within the requested tenant/Site to an `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` publication with the same fixture/spec ID **and version**. Return all distinct publication IDs and per-ID provenance. Different fixture IDs or versions, or a combination of designated and undesignated IDs, is `MIXED`. An empty citation set, no designated IDs, or any missing, foreign-Site or broken accepted-ID/publication link is `UNKNOWN`; a broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`, and the read names the problematic IDs. An accepted ID with no designation is unknown authorship, not proof of a real source.

Compute a Finding from its selected immutable FindingRevision evidence set. Compute each consequence revision from the union of that selected FindingRevision set and that consequence revision's own quantified power-interval accepted IDs. Report the two sets and their IDs separately so a later consequence can have a different state; never inherit the current head's label for historical revisions.

**Packet change:** add a precise set-state truth table, including two publications with one fixture/version, differing versions, empty set, missing/foreign link and consequence-only mixed input. Require response fields for all publication IDs, per-evidence provenance, problematic IDs and exact selected revision IDs.

## Q3 - unknown source and money: accept with gate precedence

`MIXED` or `UNKNOWN` provenance blocks a **current displayed amount** on Finding Financials, consequence and S5 Overview, even if a stored consequence says `CURRENT PRICED` or LR-01 money eligibility says `ELIGIBLE`. Keep any old value reachable only as explicitly historical/audit material with its exact revision, source state and limitation; it is not a current amount. Source provenance is one independent gate: an all-authored set may show current money only when LR-01 eligibility, exact selected Finding/consequence basis, currentness, source-open and ordinary price/quantity gates also pass. If several gates fail, expose their typed reasons without hiding the source problem. Do not treat unknown as real measurements or as zero cost. Keep `Demonstration data` only for the fully authored case. Mixed/unknown copy remains proposed for the owner at the W1 checkpoint; this ruling does not approve wording or pilot designation.

**Packet change:** state the gate composition and audit-only historical behavior for all three money reads, add tests for `CURRENT PRICED` plus `UNKNOWN`/`MIXED`, LR `ELIGIBLE` plus source refusal, and S5 composition after its merge. Include the owner-visible copy and pilot designation in the checkpoint handoff.

## PostgreSQL writer and rule 8

This extends `evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py`, the existing ledger writer; it creates no new writer. Add the publication table and any separate binding table to the ledger's rule-8 ownership allowlist **for INSERT only**. If binding is instead a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id`, set it only in the batch INSERT during admission; never permit an UPDATE to add or change it. Rule 8 must reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/upsert/DDL on publication or link rows from the ledger and reject their writes from every other module. Preserve existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver/write non-vacuity, including any independently merged writer when implementation starts. Back this up with database uniqueness, scoped foreign keys and immutability enforcement so direct SQL cannot change publication/link rows; static guard alone is insufficient. Migration owns DDL, not a runtime writer. If LR-01 or another merged slice takes migration 0014 first, re-chain and renumber on the actual single head.

**Packet change:** name the INSERT-only rule-8 and database immutability proof for whichever binding design is chosen. Add permitted-ledger-INSERT, forbidden-other-writer-INSERT, ledger/other UPDATE/DELETE, upsert, omitted-writer/import and client-route designation probes to phase 1. Do not weaken existing eight-writer protections; account for the Action writer if merged before this implementation.

## Follow-up (plan review M1)

The blanket `UNKNOWN` default is intentional for unbound historical rows and genuinely unknown or broken input, but not for every future ordinary simulated run. Separate source class from authorship. S4-05 must support two positive, immutable, server-authorized pre-admission batch bindings: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an identified authored fixture/spec version (P01 and the authored P02 late-power fixture), and `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for ordinary simulator output with a server-recorded run ID, immutable run identity/digest and exact tenant/Site, gateway/source, batch ID and payload digest. The latter requires a registered `SIMULATED` gateway and proof that this exact batch was produced by that recorded run; `source_mode=SIMULATED`, a gateway credential, client text, Site/day match or a private manifest alone does not grant the designation. The server may keep private scenario truth outside product evidence; the public binding carries only run identity and provenance needed for the read. Extend the same ledger publication/admission lock, append-only binding, duplicate and no-retroactive-backfill rules to this class. Do not reinterpret `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` as authored fixture or physical measurement.

Resolve each selected FindingRevision's cited accepted IDs and each consequence revision's union with its own power-interval IDs. All IDs bound to one coherent authored fixture ID/version yield `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; all IDs bound to a coherent registered simulation run yield `REGISTERED_SIMULATION`. Multiple run IDs require an explicitly recorded compatible run basis; absent that, return `MIXED`. Crossing source classes, mixing bound and unbound IDs, or conflicting fixture/version/run bases is `MIXED`. No positive binding, an empty citation set, or any missing, foreign-Site or broken link is `UNKNOWN`; a broken link takes precedence. Return exact IDs and reasons. An authored or registered-simulation set may show a current amount only after the existing LR, exact-head, currentness, source-open, quantity and price gates pass, with a truthful `Demonstration data` or `Simulated data` label respectively. `MIXED`/`UNKNOWN` show no current amount and historical values stay audit-only. Existing unbound ordinary simulated and real rows therefore remain `UNKNOWN` with no current amount; new ordinary runs need the positive binding. A real gateway, even with `source_mode=LIVE`, has no positive source designation from S4-05 and cannot show current money yet.

Create follow-on registry node `I-attested-real-source-provenance` for a server-authorized, tenant/Site and source-scoped `ATTESTED_REAL_SOURCE` designation. Its contract must name the accountable authority, physical peer/device and capture channel, credential/identity binding, exact accepted batch/evidence lineage and revocation/correction behavior; a gateway credential or `LIVE` mode alone is insufficient. Only a fully attested, coherent real cited set may become current-money eligible, still subject to all ordinary gates. Planner must add this open node to `real_pilot_requires` and the pilot install gate's checked registry before marking `I-stored-demo-provenance` resolved or installing a pilot timer. S4-05 may resolve before this follow-on after its own review and owner copy checkpoint; its resolution alone grants neither real-pilot installation nor real-source current money. W1 exit remains tied to S4-05, while real-pilot money and installation wait for the real-source node and all other pilot gates. This follow-on does not waive the separate physical-source evidence requirement.

Amend S5-01's packet in whichever slice merges second. ## Implementation contract

1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say â€œSource not confirmedâ€ with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing â€œDemonstration dataâ€ wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.

Cutover: existing accepted rows with no pre-admission publication remain `UNKNOWN`; do not backfill authorship from the old Site/day spec. The P01 positive proof must prepare its publication first, then ingest a fresh, isolated exact fixture batch and inspect its accepted IDs. A host that already holds P01 evidence must show the cautious state until a separately authorized new publication and new accepted IDs exist. Do not mutate or delete its old Evidence, Finding or consequence history.

## Architect questions

1. **Which publication moment is authoritative?** Recommend pre-admission, digest-pinned SYSTEM registration with a serialized batch-key lock (contract above); it blocks retroactive authorship and leaves gateway transport unchanged. Architect ratifies before phase 1 if another moment is required.
2. **Can several authored publications contribute one Finding?** Recommend yes when every cited ID has the same fixture/spec ID and version, while listing every distinct publication ID; differing versions or undesignated IDs make the set `MIXED`, and broken links make it `UNKNOWN`. Architect confirms the set rule before phase 2.

## Implementation contract

1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say â€œSource not confirmedâ€ with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing â€œDemonstration dataâ€ wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.

Cutover: existing accepted rows with no pre-admission publication remain `UNKNOWN`; do not backfill authorship from the old Site/day spec. The P01 positive proof must prepare its publication first, then ingest a fresh, isolated exact fixture batch and inspect its accepted IDs. A host that already holds P01 evidence must show the cautious state until a separately authorized new publication and new accepted IDs exist. Do not mutate or delete its old Evidence, Finding or consequence history.

## Architect questions

1. **Which publication moment is authoritative?** Recommend pre-admission, digest-pinned SYSTEM registration with a serialized batch-key lock (contract above); it blocks retroactive authorship and leaves gateway transport unchanged. Architect ratifies before phase 1 if another moment is required.
2. **Can several authored publications contribute one Finding?** Recommend yes when every cited ID has the same fixture/spec ID and version, while listing every distinct publication ID; differing versions or undesignated IDs make the set `MIXED`, and broken links make it `UNKNOWN`. Architect confirms the set rule before phase 2.
3. **How should unknown source gate money?** Recommend the S5-01 cautious no-amount behavior for all current money reads, including Finding Financials and consequence, with audit-only historical values still linked. Architect confirms precedence against existing `CURRENT PRICED` and LR eligibility before phase 2.
**Packet change:** add a precise set-state truth table, including two publications with one fixture/version, differing versions, empty set, missing/foreign link and consequence-only mixed input. Require response fields for all publication IDs, per-evidence provenance, problematic IDs and exact selected revision IDs.

## Q3 - unknown source and money: accept with gate precedence

`MIXED` or `UNKNOWN` provenance blocks a **current displayed amount** on Finding Financials, consequence and S5 Overview, even if a stored consequence says `CURRENT PRICED` or LR-01 money eligibility says `ELIGIBLE`. Keep any old value reachable only as explicitly historical/audit material with its exact revision, source state and limitation; it is not a current amount. Source provenance is one independent gate: an all-authored set may show current money only when LR-01 eligibility, exact selected Finding/consequence basis, currentness, source-open and ordinary price/quantity gates also pass. If several gates fail, expose their typed reasons without hiding the source problem. Do not treat unknown as real measurements or as zero cost. Keep `Demonstration data` only for the fully authored case. Mixed/unknown copy remains proposed for the owner at the W1 checkpoint; this ruling does not approve wording or pilot designation.

**Packet change:** state the gate composition and audit-only historical behavior for all three money reads, add tests for `CURRENT PRICED` plus `UNKNOWN`/`MIXED`, LR `ELIGIBLE` plus source refusal, and S5 composition after its merge. Include the owner-visible copy and pilot designation in the checkpoint handoff.

## PostgreSQL writer and rule 8

This extends `evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py`, the existing ledger writer; it creates no new writer. Add the publication table and any separate binding table to the ledger's rule-8 ownership allowlist **for INSERT only**. If binding is instead a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id`, set it only in the batch INSERT during admission; never permit an UPDATE to add or change it. Rule 8 must reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/upsert/DDL on publication or link rows from the ledger and reject their writes from every other module. Preserve existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver/write non-vacuity, including any independently merged writer when implementation starts. Back this up with database uniqueness, scoped foreign keys and immutability enforcement so direct SQL cannot change publication/link rows; static guard alone is insufficient. Migration owns DDL, not a runtime writer. If LR-01 or another merged slice takes migration 0014 first, re-chain and renumber on the actual single head.

## Follow-up (plan review M1)

The blanket `UNKNOWN` default is intentional for unbound historical rows and genuinely unknown or broken input, but not for every future ordinary simulated run. Separate source class from authorship. S4-05 must support two positive, immutable, server-authorized pre-admission batch bindings: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an identified authored fixture/spec version (P01 and the authored P02 late-power fixture), and `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for ordinary simulator output with a server-recorded run ID, immutable run identity/digest and exact tenant/Site, gateway/source, batch ID and payload digest. The latter requires a registered `SIMULATED` gateway and proof that this exact batch was produced by that recorded run; `source_mode=SIMULATED`, a gateway credential, client text, Site/day match or a private manifest alone does not grant the designation. The server may keep private scenario truth outside product evidence; the public binding carries only run identity and provenance needed for the read. Extend the same ledger publication/admission lock, append-only binding, duplicate and no-retroactive-backfill rules to this class. Do not reinterpret `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` as authored fixture or physical measurement.

Resolve each selected FindingRevision's cited accepted IDs and each consequence revision's union with its own power-interval IDs. All IDs bound to one coherent authored fixture ID/version yield `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; all IDs bound to a coherent registered simulation run yield `REGISTERED_SIMULATION`. Multiple run IDs require an explicitly recorded compatible run basis; absent that, return `MIXED`. Crossing source classes, mixing bound and unbound IDs, or conflicting fixture/version/run bases is `MIXED`. No positive binding, an empty citation set, or any missing, foreign-Site or broken link is `UNKNOWN`; a broken link takes precedence. Return exact IDs and reasons. An authored or registered-simulation set may show a current amount only after the existing LR, exact-head, currentness, source-open, quantity and price gates pass, with a truthful `Demonstration data` or `Simulated data` label respectively. `MIXED`/`UNKNOWN` show no current amount and historical values stay audit-only. Existing unbound ordinary simulated and real rows therefore remain `UNKNOWN` with no current amount; new ordinary runs need the positive binding. A real gateway, even with `source_mode=LIVE`, has no positive source designation from S4-05 and cannot show current money yet.

"""Installation gate for the S4-02d environment schedule tick (D-2026-10-14-s402d-schedule-storage-and-install-gate).

    python tools/schedule-install-gate.py --host-class private|walkthrough|demo|pilot [--registry PATH]

Installs nothing. It reads the delivery registry and says whether a persistent tick timer may be installed for the
host class, printing the reason; exit 0 when open, 2 when closed.

- `private`: a developer's private database; open (optional one-minute tick, the per-Site timer removed).
- `walkthrough`: an isolated walkthrough database; never a timer (explicit `tick` invocations only); exit 2.
- `demo`: owner-visible; open only when `I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit` is `resolved`.
- `pilot`: a real-Site pilot; open only when that node and every `real_pilot_requires` node are `resolved`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
REGISTRY = ROOT / "frontend" / "docs" / "architecture" / "v69-dependency-registry-pilot.json"
F1 = "I-late-reading-series-and-money-limit"


def decide(registry: dict, host_class: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    status = {n["id"]: n.get("status") for n in registry.get("nodes", [])}
    if host_class == "private":
        return True, "private development database: an optional one-minute tick is allowed; remove the per-Site timer"
    if host_class == "walkthrough":
        return False, "isolated walkthrough database: explicit tick invocations only, no persistent timer"
    needed = [F1] + (list(registry.get("real_pilot_requires") or []) if host_class == "pilot" else [])
    needed = list(dict.fromkeys(n if isinstance(n, str) else n.get("id") for n in needed))  # F1 is listed once
    open_ = [f"{n} ({status.get(n, 'missing')})" for n in needed if status.get(n) != "resolved"]
    if open_:
        return False, (f"{host_class} host is owner-visible or real: do not install the tick until resolved: "
                       + ", ".join(open_))
    return True, f"{host_class} host: gate nodes resolved ({', '.join(needed)}); install one timer and retire the " \
                 "per-Site consequence timer (backend/README-db.md)"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="schedule-install-gate")
    parser.add_argument("--host-class", required=True, choices=("private", "walkthrough", "demo", "pilot"))
    parser.add_argument("--registry", default=str(REGISTRY))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    registry = json.loads(Path(args.registry).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ok, reason = decide(registry, args.host_class)
    print(("OPEN: " if ok else "CLOSED: ") + reason)
    return 0 if ok else 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

-## Implementation contract
-
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.

-## Implementation contract
-
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.

The P01 positive proof must prepare its publication first, then ingest a fresh, isolated exact fixture batch and inspect its accepted IDs. A host that already holds P01 evidence must show the cautious state until a separately authorized new publication and new accepted IDs exist. Do not mutate or delete its old Evidence, Finding or consequence history.

+## Shared contract
 
-- `backend/migrations/versions/0005_evidence_ledger.py:116-145,161-210` has tenant/Site-scoped `ingestion_batch`, `accepted_evidence`, `batch_id` and composite foreign keys, but no publication author or fixture version. `source_mode` is `LIVE|SIMULATED`, not proof of authorship. `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/ledger.py:368-413` defines the ledger contract.
-- `backend/assetops_backend/evidence_api.py:264-275,287-345` authenticates a registered gateway for V2 `POST /api/ingestion/batches`; this principal only permits upload. `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py:202-240,242-307,309-327` opens a digest-pinned batch and atomically persists accepted evidence/dispositions in chunks. It is the **existing writer to extend**; no ninth writer is proposed.
-- `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/adapters/postgres_finding_store.py:161-204,308-330` stores exact `finding_revision_evidence` IDs and reads their lineage. `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/finding_read.py:350-438,446-550` exposes selected revision and Evidence reads. `backend/assetops_backend/financials/consequence_read.py:87-132,149-221` exposes consequence versions with power-interval evidence IDs and current amount status. `backend/assetops_backend/finding_api.py:247-277,284-308` serves the consequence and Financials routes.
-- The retiring heuristic is `backend/assetops_backend/demonstration_label.py:36-45,60-77`: it loads an on-disk case spec and labels solely by Site code and UTC day, or “Source not confirmed” when unreadable. `backend/assetops_backend/finding_api.py:275-276,306` calls it on both money reads; `frontend/src/sites/FindingConsequence.tsx:115,443` displays the returned label. `backend/tests/test_s4_assumption_read_api.py:269-307` asserts the old behavior; replace those assertions with stored-provenance cases.
-- `tools/checks/configuration-persistence.ps1:621-625,678-704,828-840` rule 8 owns the ledger table allowlist and rejects other runtime database writers/driver imports. `backend/assetops_backend/publish_assumption.py:1-4,104-164` is an existing SYSTEM-only *pattern*, not a provenance publisher. `backend/TESTING.md:7-29` requires focused phase tests and one final-revision real-Postgres suite; `tools/check-all.ps1:64` invokes the registry checker (`frontend/docs/architecture/check_v69_dependency_registry.cjs:2`).
+1. A server-side SYSTEM command registers `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` with fixture/spec ID **and version** (authored P01 and P02) or `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` with server-recorded run ID, immutable run identity/digest, registered `SIMULATED` gateway, and proof the exact batch came from that run. Both pin tenant/Site UUID, gateway/source, external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, immutable publication ID, server-resolved principal, authorization basis, channel, trigger and recorded time. Private scenario truth stays outside product evidence. `SIMULATED`/`LIVE`, credential, client text, Site/day match or private manifest alone confers no designation. No public designation route.
+2. Registration and `open_batch` take the **same transaction-scoped advisory lock** on the scoped tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch key and check admission under it. Identical retries return the same ID; changed content or publication-ID reuse fails. Registration after *any* admission, including partial admission, fails. `open_batch` binds only the exact preauthorized digest/identity commitment in its admission transaction; matching key with mismatched commitment fails rather than downgrading to unknown. Unpublished upload remains accepted with unknown source. Accepted IDs inherit immutable batch linkage across chunk restart; duplicate disposition retains its original accepted ID/provenance; rejected/conflict rows acquire none. No retroactive assignment or Site/day backfill.
+3. Resolve each selected FindingRevision's immutable cited accepted-ID set. Resolve each consequence revision separately from the union of that FindingRevision set and **its own quantified power-interval accepted IDs**. Return `finding_revision_id`, `consequence_revision_id` where applicable, exact cited/power/union IDs, per-evidence `accepted_evidence_id`, `batch_id`, `publication_id`, `source_class`, fixture ID/version or run ID/basis, all distinct publication IDs, `problematic_accepted_evidence_ids`, state and typed reasons. Historical revisions retain their own state.
 
-## Implementation contract
+| Scoped citation set | State / reason |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to authored publications with same fixture ID/version, including several publication IDs | `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; list every publication ID |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to one run, or several runs with explicitly recorded compatible run basis | `REGISTERED_SIMULATION`; list run/publication IDs |
+| Different authored fixture/version; incompatible runs; crossed classes; bound and unbound mixed; consequence-only power conflicts | `MIXED` with exact IDs and basis reason |
+| Empty; no positive binding; missing, foreign-Site or broken accepted-ID/publication link | `UNKNOWN` with exact IDs/reasons; broken link precedes `MIXED` |
 
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.
+4. Authored and registered-simulation sets can show current money only after **all** LR eligibility, exact selected Finding/consequence basis, currentness, source-open, quantity and price gates pass. Show `Demonstration data` or `Simulated data` respectively. `MIXED`/`UNKNOWN` block current amount on all three money reads; expose `MIXED_OR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` alongside every other failed typed gate. Old amount is audit-only with exact revision, source state and limitation; unknown means neither physical measurement nor zero cost. Later `ATTESTED_REAL_SOURCE` may qualify only a coherent fully attested cited set subject to the same gates.
+5. S5-01 packet amendment is mandatory in **whichever of S4-05b and S5-01 merges second**: replace `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39`'s `demonstration_case`/unreadable-spec trigger with stored exact-revision provenance; add authored, registered-simulation, mixed, unknown and later attested-real classes; apply `MIXED_OR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` for mixed/unknown regardless of spec readability, including consequence-only power; preserve IDs and simultaneous reasons. Update P01/P02, positively bound ordinary simulation and unbound-history walkthrough expectations. Source class does not influence S5 Finding choice. Compose at LR-01's `financials/money_eligibility.py` and `finding_api.py:347` bridge after its merge; re-chain migration from the then-current single head (LR-01 may take 0014/0015, making this 0016).
 
-Cutover: existing accepted rows with no pre-admission publication remain `UNKNOWN`; do not backfill authorship from the old Site/day spec. The P01 positive proof must prepare its publication first, then ingest a fresh, isolated exact fixture batch and inspect its accepted IDs. A host that already holds P01 evidence must show the cautious state until a separately authorized new publication and new accepted IDs exist. Do not mutate or delete its old Evidence, Finding or consequence history.

It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.
+4. Authored and registered-simulation sets can show current money only after **all** LR eligibility, exact selected Finding/consequence basis, currentness, source-open, quantity and price gates pass. Show `Demonstration data` or `Simulated data` respectively. `MIXED`/`UNKNOWN` block current amount on all three money reads; expose `MIXED_OR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` alongside every other failed typed gate. Old amount is audit-only with exact revision, source state and limitation; unknown means neither physical measurement nor zero cost. +| Empty; no positive binding; missing, foreign-Site or broken accepted-ID/publication link | `UNKNOWN` with exact IDs/reasons; broken link precedes `MIXED` |
 
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. -- `backend/migrations/versions/0005_evidence_ledger.py:116-145,161-210` has tenant/Site-scoped `ingestion_batch`, `accepted_evidence`, `batch_id` and composite foreign keys, but no publication author or fixture version. `source_mode` is `LIVE|SIMULATED`, not proof of authorship. `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/ledger.py:368-413` defines the ledger contract.
-- `backend/assetops_backend/evidence_api.py:264-275,287-345` authenticates a registered gateway for V2 `POST /api/ingestion/batches`; this principal only permits upload. `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py:202-240,242-307,309-327` opens a digest-pinned batch and atomically persists accepted evidence/dispositions in chunks. It is the **existing writer to extend**; no ninth writer is proposed.
-- `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/adapters/postgres_finding_store.py:161-204,308-330` stores exact `finding_revision_evidence` IDs and reads their lineage. `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/finding_read.py:350-438,446-550` exposes selected revision and Evidence reads. `backend/assetops_backend/financials/consequence_read.py:87-132,149-221` exposes consequence versions with power-interval evidence IDs and current amount status. `backend/assetops_backend/finding_api.py:247-277,284-308` serves the consequence and Financials routes.
-- The retiring heuristic is `backend/assetops_backend/demonstration_label.py:36-45,60-77`: it loads an on-disk case spec and labels solely by Site code and UTC day, or “Source not confirmed” when unreadable. `backend/assetops_backend/finding_api.py:275-276,306` calls it on both money reads; `frontend/src/sites/FindingConsequence.tsx:115,443` displays the returned label. `backend/tests/test_s4_assumption_read_api.py:269-307` asserts the old behavior; replace those assertions with stored-provenance cases.
-- `tools/checks/configuration-persistence.ps1:621-625,678-704,828-840` rule 8 owns the ledger table allowlist and rejects other runtime database writers/driver imports. `backend/assetops_backend/publish_assumption.py:1-4,104-164` is an existing SYSTEM-only *pattern*, not a provenance publisher. `backend/TESTING.md:7-29` requires focused phase tests and one final-revision real-Postgres suite; `tools/check-all.ps1:64` invokes the registry checker (`frontend/docs/architecture/check_v69_dependency_registry.cjs:2`).
+1. A server-side SYSTEM command registers `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` with fixture/spec ID **and version** (authored P01 and P02) or `REGISTERED_SIMULATION` with server-recorded run ID, immutable run identity/digest, registered `SIMULATED` gateway, and proof the exact batch came from that run. Both pin tenant/Site UUID, gateway/source, external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, immutable publication ID, server-resolved principal, authorization basis, channel, trigger and recorded time. Private scenario truth stays outside product evidence. `SIMULATED`/`LIVE`, credential, client text, Site/day match or private manifest alone confers no designation. No public designation route.
+2. Registration and `open_batch` take the **same transaction-scoped advisory lock** on the scoped tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch key and check admission under it. Identical retries return the same ID; changed content or publication-ID reuse fails. Registration after *any* admission, including partial admission, fails. `open_batch` binds only the exact preauthorized digest/identity commitment in its admission transaction; matching key with mismatched commitment fails rather than downgrading to unknown. Unpublished upload remains accepted with unknown source. Accepted IDs inherit immutable batch linkage across chunk restart; duplicate disposition retains its original accepted ID/provenance; rejected/conflict rows acquire none. No retroactive assignment or Site/day backfill.
+3. Resolve each selected FindingRevision's immutable cited accepted-ID set. Resolve each consequence revision separately from the union of that FindingRevision set and **its own quantified power-interval accepted IDs**. Return `finding_revision_id`, `consequence_revision_id` where applicable, exact cited/power/union IDs, per-evidence `accepted_evidence_id`, `batch_id`, `publication_id`, `source_class`, fixture ID/version or run ID/basis, all distinct publication IDs, `problematic_accepted_evidence_ids`, state and typed reasons. Historical revisions retain their own state.
 
-## Implementation contract
+| Scoped citation set | State / reason |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to authored publications with same fixture ID/version, including several publication IDs | `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; list every publication ID |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to one run, or several runs with explicitly recorded compatible run basis | `REGISTERED_SIMULATION`; list run/publication IDs |
+| Different authored fixture/version; incompatible runs; crossed classes; bound and unbound mixed; consequence-only power conflicts | `MIXED` with exact IDs and basis reason |
+| Empty; no positive binding; missing, foreign-Site or broken accepted-ID/publication link | `UNKNOWN` with exact IDs/reasons; broken link precedes `MIXED` |
 
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. The accepted evidence already references the scoped batch (`0005:165,197-200`); expose the immutable publication ID per **accepted evidence ID** through that link, including interrupted/resumed chunks. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.
-4. **Read and amount rules (new).** Resolve every cited accepted ID under the requested tenant/Site, returning publication ID, designation and fixture/spec version per record plus a set-level state: `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` only when every relevant cited ID is bound to a consistent authored publication basis; `MIXED` when some cited IDs have that designation and others have no designation or a different basis; `UNKNOWN` when none is designated or any cited ID/link cannot be resolved (and retain exact problematic IDs). A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Preserve `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39-41` no-amount rule when its branch merges. Keep existing “Demonstration data” wording for fully authored P01; propose concise mixed/unknown copy to owner at checkpoint. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity. Add guard probes for permitted ledger INSERT, forbidden other-writer INSERT, mutation, omitted writer/import, and client route attempting designation. If LR-01 merges first and contributes migrations 0014/0015 on its branch, re-chain this migration to the new head and renumber it; never create a parallel head. Recheck S5-01 read composition after its merge without stacking this task on that unmerged branch.
+4. Authored and registered-simulation sets can show current money only after **all** LR eligibility, exact selected Finding/consequence basis, currentness, source-open, quantity and price gates pass. Show `Demonstration data` or `Simulated data` respectively. `MIXED`/`UNKNOWN` block current amount on all three money reads; expose `MIXED_OR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` alongside every other failed typed gate. Old amount is audit-only with exact revision, source state and limitation; unknown means neither physical measurement nor zero cost. Later `ATTESTED_REAL_SOURCE` may qualify only a coherent fully attested cited set subject to the same gates.
+5. S5-01 packet amendment is mandatory in **whichever of S4-05b and S5-01 merges second**: replace `tasks/S5-01-site-overview.md:39`'s `demonstration_case`/unreadable-spec trigger with stored exact-revision provenance; add authored, registered-simulation, mixed, unknown and later attested-real classes; apply `MIXED_OR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` for mixed/unknown regardless of spec readability, including consequence-only power; preserve IDs and simultaneous reasons. Update P01/P02, positively bound ordinary simulation and unbound-history walkthrough expectations. Source class does not influence S5 Finding choice. Compose at LR-01's `financials/money_eligibility.py` and `finding_api.py:347` bridge after its merge; re-chain migration from the then-current single head (LR-01 may take 0014/0015, making this 0016).
 
-Cutover: existing accepted rows with no pre-admission publication remain `UNKNOWN`; do not backfill authorship from the old Site/day spec.     if (!['S', 'M', 'L'].includes(node.effort)) fail(`${node.id}: missing effort size`);
    if (node.status === 'resolved' && !node.evidence) fail(`${node.id}: resolved without evidence`);
    if (node.kind === 'implementation' && !['task', 'persistence', 'projection', 'ui', 'edge', 'producer', 'ingestion'].includes(node.layer)) fail(`${node.id}: missing implementation layer`);
  }
  nodes.set(node.id, node);
}

const visiting = new Set();
const visited = new Set();
function visit(id) {
  if (visiting.has(id)) fail(`Dependency cycle at ${id}`);
  if (visited.has(id)) return;
  const node = nodes.get(id);
  if (!node) fail(`Unknown node ${id}`);
  visiting.add(id);
  for (const dependency of node.requires) {
    if (!nodes.has(dependency)) fail(`${id}: unknown dependency ${dependency}`);
    if (nodes.get(dependency).kind === 'product') fail(`${id}: product node used as prerequisite`);
    visit(dependency);
  }

-## Implementation contract
+| Scoped citation set | State / reason |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to authored publications with same fixture ID/version, including several publication IDs | `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; list every publication ID |
+| Nonempty; every ID bound to one run, or several runs with explicitly recorded compatible run basis | `REGISTERED_SIMULATION`; list run/publication IDs |
+| Different authored fixture/version; incompatible runs; crossed classes; bound and unbound mixed; consequence-only power conflicts | `MIXED` with exact IDs and basis reason |
+| Empty; no positive binding; missing, foreign-Site or broken accepted-ID/publication link | `UNKNOWN` with exact IDs/reasons; broken link precedes `MIXED` |
 
-1. **Publication, before upload (new).** Add migration `0014` from main's `0013_schedule_state` head for an append-only `evidence_publication` table and a scoped immutable batch-publication binding (either a nullable `ingestion_batch.publication_id` or a one-to-one insert-only link). Publication has UUID ID; tenant/Site UUID; external batch ID, canonical Batch V2 payload SHA-256, gateway/source IDs; designation `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION`; fixture/spec ID and version; server-resolved `actor_kind=SYSTEM`, stable service principal, authorization basis, source channel, triggering job/fixture ID, and server `recorded_at`. Use composite tenant/Site FKs, unique publication identity and unique exact batch commitment; prohibit update/delete or conflicting reuse. A real/live assertion is **not** inferred from absence of designation or `source_mode=LIVE`.
-2. **Authorization (new).** Expose only a server-side administrative SYSTEM fixture/CLI command with fixed service principal and explicit configured allowlist/authorization basis, modelled on `publish_assumption.py`; no public gateway or browser write route. It must validate fixture/spec identity/version and canonical batch digest against the exact payload, then insert the publication through an extension of `PostgresEvidenceLedger`. No `--actor`, `--author` or client-supplied provenance text can become authority. Refuse wrong tenant/Site, gateway/source, missing or conflicting batch digest, publication ID reuse with changed content, and publication after any batch admission. An identical retry returns the same publication. Registration and subsequent `open_batch` must serialize for the same scoped batch key so ingestion cannot race an after-the-fact designation. The upload remains valid without designation but has `UNKNOWN` authorship.
-3. **Accepted binding (new).** `open_batch` matches only the preauthorized exact tenant/Site/gateway/source/external-batch-ID/digest commitment. A duplicate disposition retains the original accepted ID and its original provenance; it cannot relabel old evidence. Rejected/conflict rows confer no provenance. No retroactive assignment or mutable backfill of historic accepted rows. Fail the upload if a matching publication conflicts; never silently downgrade a claimed publication to unknown.

A broken link takes precedence over `MIXED`. A FindingRevision uses its immutable cited set, not an episode date. A consequence uses its **own** quantified power-interval evidence IDs as well as the selected FindingRevision cited set; a later revision can differ. Preserve historical revision-specific results; do not relabel a historical revision from the current head. Mixed/unknown reads say “Source not confirmed” with exact IDs and show no current amount wherever this source gate is used. Remove runtime calls to `demonstration_case` and its date/spec cache; retain its old test only as regression proving same-day real/unknown is not labelled authored.
-5. **Writer and migration boundary.** Extend the existing ledger writer's allowed tables in rule 8 (`configuration-persistence.ps1:624-625`); require INSERT only for publication/link rows, and prevent ledger or other writers from UPDATE/DELETE of these immutable rows. Preserve all eight existing writer allowlists, reverse ownership and driver non-vacuity.
